## Overview

`cooccure` builds co-occurrence networks, in which two items are linked
when they appear in the same transaction: the keywords of one article,
the genres of one film, the actors of one cast, the codes of one
interview passage, or the states of one learning session. The network
shows which items tend to go together and how a field, a corpus or a set
of sessions is organized around them. The weight of a link starts as the
number of shared transactions. Because frequent items co-occur often by
chance alone, the weight can be normalized for item frequency by one of
eight similarity measures, such as association strength or the Jaccard
index (van Eck & Waltman, 2009), and each transaction’s contribution can
be counted fractionally (Perianes-Rodriguez et al., 2016). One network
can be built per group, for example per decade, and the networks
compared.

All of this is done by one function,
[`cooccurrence()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/cooccurrence.md).
It reads delimited columns, long (item, transaction) tables, binary and
one-hot tables, wide sequences, lists of vectors and event logs; sliding
windows turn ordered sequences into transactions. It returns a tidy edge
list with a weight and a raw count per pair, which converts to the
network classes of igraph, tidygraph, cograph and Nestimate.

## Method

Let $`B`$ be the transaction-by-item incidence matrix, with
$`B_{ti} = 1`$ when item $`i`$ occurs in transaction $`t`$. The
co-occurrence counts are $`C = B^\top B`$, with the diagonal set to
zero, and $`f_i`$ is the number of transactions containing item $`i`$.
Similarity measures rescale $`C_{ij}`$ by the frequencies (van Eck &
Waltman, 2009):

| `similarity`    | Weight of the edge $`i`$–$`j`$        |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------|
| `"none"`        | $`C_{ij}`$                            |
| `"jaccard"`     | $`C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j - C_{ij})`$     |
| `"cosine"`      | $`C_{ij} / \sqrt{f_i f_j}`$           |
| `"inclusion"`   | $`C_{ij} / \min(f_i, f_j)`$           |
| `"association"` | $`C_{ij} / (f_i f_j)`$                |
| `"dice"`        | $`2 C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j)`$            |
| `"equivalence"` | $`C_{ij}^2 / (f_i f_j)`$              |
| `"relative"`    | $`C_{ij} / \sum_k C_{ik}`$ (directed) |

With fractional counting each transaction of $`n`$ items contributes
$`1/(n-1)`$ to each of its pairs instead of 1 (Perianes-Rodriguez et
al., 2016); with attention counting a pair contributes
$`\exp(-|p_i - p_j| / \lambda)`$, decaying with the distance between the
two positions in an ordered transaction. Every measure except
`"relative"` gives an undirected network; `"relative"` divides each row
by its sum, so its edges have a direction and the edge list holds one
row per direction.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("cooccure")

# development version
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mohsaqr/cooccure")
```

## Examples

`movies` holds 1,000 highly rated films with their genres in one
comma-separated column. Genres are linked when they are assigned to the
same film, and Jaccard similarity discounts the most common genres.

``` r

library(cooccure)

genres <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                       similarity = "jaccard", min_occur = 20)
print(genres, n = 6)
#> # cooccurrence: 17 nodes, 102 edges | density: 0.7500 | mean degree: 12.0000 | 998 transactions
#> # similarity: jaccard | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 136 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: Drama(deg=16,str=1.153), Comedy(deg=16,str=0.8949), Romance(deg=15,str=0.5377), Action(deg=14,str=1.009), Adventure(deg=14,str=0.8788)
#>       from          to weight count
#>  Adventure   Animation  0.285    39
#>     Action       Crime  0.237    59
#>     Comedy       Drama  0.211   159
#>     Action   Adventure  0.208    44
#>  Biography Documentary  0.204    44
#>      Drama     Romance  0.198   131
#> # ... 96 more edges
```

The weight matrix can be drawn as a heatmap.

``` r

plot(genres)
```

![Jaccard weights of the genre
network.](reference/figures/README-heatmap-1.png)

Jaccard weights of the genre network.

`split_by` builds one network per decade, and the group table compares
them.

``` r

by_decade <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                          split_by = "decade", similarity = "jaccard",
                          min_occur = 5)
as.data.frame(by_decade, what = "groups")
#>   group n_nodes n_edges possible_edges density weight_mean count_sum
#> 1 1970s      12      34             66   0.515      0.1334       136
#> 2 1980s      14      43             91   0.473      0.0977       164
#> 3 1990s      13      39             78   0.500      0.1126       187
#> 4 2000s      16      66            120   0.550      0.0769       335
#> 5 2010s      17      85            136   0.625      0.0666       581
#> 6 2020s      13      39             78   0.500      0.1004       184
```

`actors` is a long table with one row per actor and film; actors in the
same film are linked, giving a collaboration network. One decade of a
split network converts to `igraph` with `group =`.

``` r

cast <- cooccurrence(actors, field = "actor", by = "tconst",
                     split_by = "decade", min_occur = 2)
summary(as_igraph(cast, group = "2010s"))
#> IGRAPH ab8d353 UNW- 145 756 -- 
#> + attr: name (v/c), weight (e/n), count (e/n)
```

## Authors and citation

`cooccure` is written by [Mohammed Saqr](https://saqr.me), [Sonsoles
López-Pernas](https://sonsoles.me) and Kamila Misiejuk. Mohammed Saqr
maintains the package. Questions and bug reports can be submitted
through the [repository issue
tracker](https://github.com/mohsaqr/cooccure/issues). The package
citation is available through `citation("cooccure")`.

The bundled `movies`, `actors` and `actor_genres` data are derived from
the IMDb non-commercial datasets
(<https://data.imdb.com/non-commercial-datasets/>).

### References

Perianes-Rodriguez, A., Waltman, L., & van Eck, N. J. (2016).
Constructing bibliometric networks: A comparison between full and
fractional counting. *Journal of Informetrics*, *10*(4), 1178–1195.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joi.2016.10.006>

Saqr, M., López-Pernas, S., Conde, M. Á., & Hernández-García, Á. (2024).
Social network analysis: A primer, a guide and a tutorial in R. In M.
Saqr & S. López-Pernas (Eds.), *Learning analytics methods and
tutorials: A practical guide using R*. Springer.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-54464-4_15>

van Eck, N. J., & Waltman, L. (2009). How to normalize cooccurrence
data? An analysis of some well-known similarity measures. *Journal of
the American Society for Information Science and Technology*, *60*(8),
1635–1651. <https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.21075>

# Package index

## Overview

- [`cooccure`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/cooccure-package.md)
  [`cooccure-package`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/cooccure-package.md)
  : cooccure: co-occurrence networks from many kinds of data

## Building networks

Co-occurrence networks from delimited columns, long tables, one-hot
tables, sequences and event logs, with similarity, counting, scaling,
filtering and groups.

- [`cooccurrence()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/cooccurrence.md)
  [`co()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/cooccurrence.md)
  : Build a co-occurrence network

## Results

Printing, summarizing and plotting a network, and its edge, node and
group tables.

- [`print(`*`<cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/print.cooccurrence.md)
  : Print a co-occurrence network
- [`summary(`*`<cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/summary.cooccurrence.md)
  : Summarize a co-occurrence network
- [`print(`*`<summary.cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/print.summary.cooccurrence.md)
  : Print a co-occurrence network summary
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as.data.frame.cooccurrence.md)
  : Extract the tables of a co-occurrence network
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<summary.cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as.data.frame.summary.cooccurrence.md)
  : Extract the tables of a co-occurrence network summary
- [`plot(`*`<cooccurrence>`*`)`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/plot.cooccurrence.md)
  : Plot a co-occurrence network

## Conversion

The weight matrix and the network classes of igraph, tidygraph, cograph
and Nestimate.

- [`as_matrix()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as_matrix.md)
  : Extract the weight matrix of a co-occurrence network
- [`as_igraph()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as_igraph.md)
  : Convert a co-occurrence network to an igraph graph
- [`as_tidygraph()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as_tidygraph.md)
  : Convert a co-occurrence network to a tidygraph
- [`as_cograph()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as_cograph.md)
  : Convert a co-occurrence network to a cograph network
- [`as_netobject()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/as_netobject.md)
  : Convert a co-occurrence network to a Nestimate netobject

## Data

Films, casts and genres from the IMDb non-commercial datasets, and a
small cast table.

- [`movies`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/movies.md) :
  Highly rated films with their genres (IMDb, 1970-2024)
- [`actors`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/actors.md) :
  Actors and the films they appeared in (IMDb, 1970-2024)
- [`actor_genres`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/actor_genres.md)
  : Actors and the genres of their films (IMDb, 1970-2024)
- [`demo`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/demo.md) : A
  small cast table of ten films

## Explorer

An interactive application for building networks.

- [`launch_app()`](https://pak.dynasite.org/cooccure/reference/launch_app.md)
  : Open the interactive co-occurrence explorer
